texts.orig: What does a growth team do?
texts.text: What does a growth team do?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Growth teams don’t build net new products or features. Instead, they work on creating distribution strategies that help acquire, activate, engage, and monetize customers on the existing product value.
texts.text: Growth teams don’t build net new products or features. Instead, they work on creating distribution strategies that help acquire, activate, engage, and monetize customers on the existing product value.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most product and marketing teams are built to create or expand the core value provided to customers. Growth is connecting more people to the existing value.
texts.text: Most product and marketing teams are built to create or expand the core value provided to customers. Growth is connecting more people to the existing value.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: How does growth look at different company stages?
texts.text: How does growth look at different company stages?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Growth efforts and team compositions vary depending on the stage of a company’s development. Just like with the first product or marketing hire, it is a difficult decision to determine when growth specialization and hiring are worthwhile. Here are our guidelines:
texts.text: Growth efforts and team compositions vary depending on the stage of a company’s development. Just like with the first product or marketing hire, it is a difficult decision to determine when growth specialization and hiring are worthwhile. Here are our guidelines:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Before PMF: Develop a growth model hypothesis
texts.text: Before PMF: Develop a growth model hypothesis

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Many founders get caught up in growth hype and try to hire growth talent as early as possible. Don’t fall victim to this trap—you will only waste precious capital and equity for lackluster results. Growth is about increasing the distribution of the core product. If there is no validation that the product has found PMF, growth has nothing to grow. PMF has to happen first, then growth.
texts.text: Many founders get caught up in growth hype and try to hire growth talent as early as possible. Don’t fall victim to this trap—you will only waste precious capital and equity for lackluster results. Growth is about increasing the distribution of the core product. If there is no validation that the product has found PMF, growth has nothing to grow. PMF has to happen first, then growth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: But that’s not to say you shouldn’t think about growth pre-PMF. As you explore potential product-market fit, it is crucial to have hypotheses on how you will distribute your product. For example, if you are planning to be product-led, then the product has to be designed with acquisition, monetization, and retention distribution goals in mind from the very beginning. If you are planning to be marketing/sales-led, then the product experience will look very different from inception, as you will have humans responsible for growth levers and distribution.
texts.text: But that’s not to say you shouldn’t think about growth pre-PMF. As you explore potential product-market fit, it is crucial to have hypotheses on how you will distribute your product. For example, if you are planning to be product-led, then the product has to be designed with acquisition, monetization, and retention distribution goals in mind from the very beginning. If you are planning to be marketing/sales-led, then the product experience will look very different from inception, as you will have humans responsible for growth levers and distribution.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Founders must assess their PMF strategy and develop the best-fitting ways to distribute the product to create predictable, sustainable, and defensible growth. It can be product-led, marketing-led, sales-led, or combinations thereof. But just like you wouldn’t outsource your PMF to a PM, you cannot outsource your initial growth ideas.

It can be product-led, marketing-led, sales-led, or combinations thereof. But just like you wouldn’t outsource your PMF to a PM, you cannot outsource your initial growth ideas.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Finding PMF: Founder-led growth
texts.text: Finding PMF: Founder-led growth

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During early signs of traction and initial scaling stages, it is important to validate that the growth model hypothesis was correct. Founder-led growth is the best path here, where the founder drives growth efforts across product-led, marketing-led, or sales-led motions.
texts.text: During early signs of traction and initial scaling stages, it is important to validate that the growth model hypothesis was correct. Founder-led growth is the best path here, where the founder drives growth efforts across product-led, marketing-led, or sales-led motions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Product-led growth:
texts.text: Product-led growth:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The founder prioritizes not only building core functionality but product experiences to resolve distribution goals, from acquisition to monetization.
texts.text: The founder prioritizes not only building core functionality but product experiences to resolve distribution goals, from acquisition to monetization.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Marketing-led growth:
texts.text: Marketing-led growth:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The founder prototypes third-party channels and content to enable the market with the information to drive acquisition, educate on engagement, and assist monetization.
texts.text: The founder prototypes third-party channels and content to enable the market with the information to drive acquisition, educate on engagement, and assist monetization.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Sales-led growth:
texts.text: Sales-led growth:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The founder does sales themself.
texts.text: The founder does sales themself.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The benefit of founder-led growth at this stage is quick decision-making, tight alignment to vision and customer, and, perhaps most importantly, leading by example to set up the growth mindset within the company culture.
texts.text: The benefit of founder-led growth at this stage is quick decision-making, tight alignment to vision and customer, and, perhaps most importantly, leading by example to set up the growth mindset within the company culture.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: At this stage, we recommend you don’t hire a team for growth, as it’s still too early in the PMF journey to warrant multiple headcounts, but if you still want to hire dedicated growth talent, look for someone with (1) high iteration/learning velocity; (2) a growth mindset; (3) strong execution skills, and a generalist who can execute across different growth problems; and, ideally, (4) someone internal who already has the business context.
texts.text: At this stage, we recommend you don’t hire a team for growth, as it’s still too early in the PMF journey to warrant multiple headcounts, but if you still want to hire dedicated growth talent, look for someone with (1) high iteration/learning velocity; (2) a growth mindset; (3) strong execution skills, and a generalist who can execute across different growth problems; and, ideally, (4) someone internal who already has the business context.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Scaling PMF: Hire your first full-time growth roles
texts.text: Scaling PMF: Hire your first full-time growth roles

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As your company efforts transition from a search for and validation of PMF to scaling work, you can begin hiring your growth team. In other words, the right time to think about the first growth hire is when you are ready to blow up the distribution of your current product-market fit and have initial validation of your distribution methods.
texts.text: As your company efforts transition from a search for and validation of PMF to scaling work, you can begin hiring your growth team. In other words, the right time to think about the first growth hire is when you are ready to blow up the distribution of your current product-market fit and have initial validation of your distribution methods.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your first growth hire’s skill set should be anchored to the biggest growth lever that is currently experiencing friction: acquisition, activation, engagement, or monetization. Is your biggest bottleneck to growth today acquiring new users, activating those users, keeping them retained, or generating revenue?
texts.text: Your first growth hire’s skill set should be anchored to the biggest growth lever that is currently experiencing friction: acquisition, activation, engagement, or monetization. Is your biggest bottleneck to growth today acquiring new users, activating those users, keeping them retained, or generating revenue?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It is important not to hire growth team members just to “accelerate growth,” as it will likely result in a misfire. For example, if product-led growth is your main motion, hiring a marketer to accelerate growth will lead to disappointing results—because most of the growth work will need to be done in the product by the PM and eng teams. Knowing where you are experiencing friction will ensure that you have sufficient data tracking and understanding of your growth model to bring the right talent on board, enabling new hires to have a meaningful impact.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A growth leader should not be your first hire
texts.text: A growth leader should not be your first hire

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Understanding why your business is not growing is incredibly difficult. Many founders want to shortcut this by hiring a growth leader to outsource solving this problem to them. Unfortunately, even the most experienced growth leaders will take at least 6 to 12 months to understand the local problem fully. The business ecosystem is incredibly complex, and learning about products, industries, markets, customers, and internal employee dynamics is not an easy feat. When growth leaders need immediate results, they are forced to simply copy-paste from their previous experiences, often resulting in initiatives that do not produce desired outcomes.
texts.text: Understanding why your business is not growing is incredibly difficult. Many founders want to shortcut this by hiring a growth leader to outsource solving this problem to them. Unfortunately, even the most experienced growth leaders will take at least 6 to 12 months to understand the local problem fully. The business ecosystem is incredibly complex, and learning about products, industries, markets, customers, and internal employee dynamics is not an easy feat. When growth leaders need immediate results, they are forced to simply copy-paste from their previous experiences, often resulting in initiatives that do not produce desired outcomes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Sustainable growth is about evolution, not revolution. Hiring a “builder” profile (e.g. Acquisition PM, Activation PM, Monetization PM, Acquisition Growth Marketer, Retention Growth Marketer) as your first hire is a better bet. A builder is a growth generalist focused on broad tactical and execution skills within a specific domain. These are the individuals you want on your team when you are standing up growth processes and systems from the ground up.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: How to structure the growth team
texts.text: How to structure the growth team

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Since growth is a result that the whole company contributes to, the question is how to structure the growth team to accelerate growth while also ensuring that the responsibility for growth is shared across the entire organization.
texts.text: Since growth is a result that the whole company contributes to, the question is how to structure the growth team to accelerate growth while also ensuring that the responsibility for growth is shared across the entire organization.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Let’s take data analytics teams as an example. Although almost every company has data analysts, other team members also analyze data whenever possible. While the analysts may take ownership of the more complex data projects where they can provide unique insights, the entire company must take responsibility for data analytics if they want to make data-driven decisions.
texts.text: Let’s take data analytics teams as an example. Although almost every company has data analysts, other team members also analyze data whenever possible. While the analysts may take ownership of the more complex data projects where they can provide unique insights, the entire company must take responsibility for data analytics if they want to make data-driven decisions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The same concept applies to growth teams. Growth teams take accountability over growth work where they can uniquely add value, yet the entire company should continue aligning to growth outcomes.
texts.text: The same concept applies to growth teams. Growth teams take accountability over growth work where they can uniquely add value, yet the entire company should continue aligning to growth outcomes.

texts.orig: “Snyk formed a dedicated growth organization later in its journey, initially focusing on building the necessary foundation for growth work at scale and early growth hypotheses. The org was predominantly centralized, with multiple cross-functional growth pods designed to drive cultural change, establish growth practices, and maintain a platform-wide approach. Hiring team members with a specific mindset was crucial, although some personnel changes occurred in the first 12 months. Challenges included alignment due to rapid company growth and the ‘absolution effect,’ where the existence of a dedicated growth org seemed to relieve others of growth responsibility.”

texts.orig: Decentralized growth teams operate as tribes and are optimized for fostering a growth culture.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: By building a decentralized growth tribe, you can cultivate a culture of growth throughout your organization, as members from various teams come together to share their expertise and insights. This collaborative approach leads to a more holistic understanding of growth opportunities. It also fosters a sense of ownership and accountability for driving growth, ultimately leading to more sustainable and scalable growth over the long term.
texts.text: By building a decentralized growth tribe, you can cultivate a culture of growth throughout your organization, as members from various teams come together to share their expertise and insights. This collaborative approach leads to a more holistic understanding of growth opportunities. It also fosters a sense of ownership and accountability for driving growth, ultimately leading to more sustainable and scalable growth over the long term.

texts.orig: Drawbacks:
texts.text: Drawbacks:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Priorities: Conflicting priorities of their respective departments will slow down the velocity.
texts.text: Priorities: Conflicting priorities of their respective departments will slow down the velocity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Complexity: As the number of participants in a growth tribe increases, it can become more challenging to coordinate and align everyone around a common goal or objective, leading to inefficiencies and slower decision-making.
texts.text: Complexity: As the number of participants in a growth tribe increases, it can become more challenging to coordinate and align everyone around a common goal or objective, leading to inefficiencies and slower decision-making.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Communication breakdown: With participants coming from different departments or teams, miscommunication and misunderstandings can arise, particularly if there isn’t a clear and open line of communication established. This can lead to delays, missed opportunities, and even conflicts between team members.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: “At Pinterest, we started with growth product and engineering teams reporting into the head of product and the head of engineering, respectively. A couple years after forming, the decision was made to move the growth team into Marketing. It was quickly undone within six months because they realized that having a product-led-growth team report into Marketing was creating alignment issues. It was still early in Pinterest’s journey, and the core product was evolving. We found that with growth reporting into Marketing, a lot of growth product strategy was aligned with what the product was like today, and was not aligning with where it was going be six months from now. It created a communication and alignment gap.”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: At Amplitude, our growth team structure evolved from decentralized to centralized (Marketing and Product report into VP of Growth), and then back to decentralized (Growth Marketing reports into CMO; Growth Product and Analytics report into VP of Growth) over time. What we found works well for us, going from the centralized to decentralized structure, is spreading a growth mindset across the organization, especially within marketing, product, and design orgs. It also helped with getting more resourcing in areas like growth marketing, when it’s structured as a standalone team.
texts.text: At Amplitude, our growth team structure evolved from decentralized to centralized (Marketing and Product report into VP of Growth), and then back to decentralized (Growth Marketing reports into CMO; Growth Product and Analytics report into VP of Growth) over time. What we found works well for us, going from the centralized to decentralized structure, is spreading a growth mindset across the organization, especially within marketing, product, and design orgs. It also helped with getting more resourcing in areas like growth marketing, when it’s structured as a standalone team.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: At SurveyMonkey, at first, Elena ran a dedicated growth team across growth product (acquisition, activation, monetization), marketing (acquisition, engagement), and analytics teams. We operated as a lean, mean, high-velocity machine but lacked shared goals and support from the rest of the organization. At one point, we found ourselves to be solely responsible for the forecast, even though we made up less than 25% of the company, which was far from ideal. As I left the company, the growth team was split up into a cross-functional growth tribe. The goal was to instill a growth mindset across an entire organization and create shared accountability across growth outcomes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you go with the centralized growth team structure, there’s often the question of what functions related to growth should report to a growth leader. This often depends on the competency and experience of the growth leader and how that plays into the organizational dynamics.
texts.text: If you go with the centralized growth team structure, there’s often the question of what functions related to growth should report to a growth leader. This often depends on the competency and experience of the growth leader and how that plays into the organizational dynamics.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If a growth leader you already have has a strong marketing and product background, then you can have growth marketing and product teams report to this person. If the leader only has a strong data and product background but limited experience in marketing, you could have a decentralized structure where growth analytics and growth product report to a VP of Growth, and growth marketing reports to the CMO.
texts.text: If a growth leader you already have has a strong marketing and product background, then you can have growth marketing and product teams report to this person. If the leader only has a strong data and product background but limited experience in marketing, you could have a decentralized structure where growth analytics and growth product report to a VP of Growth, and growth marketing reports to the CMO.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We have seen companies oscillate between centralized and decentralized models as circumstances change.At Amplitude, we went through several iterations of the growth team. Initially, we went with a dedicated growth team that first focused on growth traffic and then took ownership of key growth areas in the core product, including activation, monetization awareness, and self-serve product feature engagement. Growth product and engineering reported into the Head of Growth; this helped us run faster and empowered the team to have more ownership in the core product, versus aligning with other product teams on every change. But we evolved into a decentralized org structure later, with each function reporting into the functional head, to spread growth mindset across the organization.

Growth product and engineering reported into the Head of Growth; this helped us run faster and empowered the team to have more ownership in the core product, versus aligning with other product teams on every change. But we evolved into a decentralized org structure later, with each function reporting into the functional head, to spread growth mindset across the organization.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When we started the growth team at SurveyMonkey, Elena ran just growth product and analytics teams. Growth marketing began reporting to her a few years later as we evolved to be a fully centralized team (reporting to the president). However, as Elena left, the team was decentralized, and a growth tribe was created.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: “Different structures are effective at varying times. Teams may transition between reporting to multiple functions, a single person, or back to a distributed approach. Success depends on whether the structure addresses the root cause at the right moment. Centralization is preferable for velocity issues, while distribution may be better for resolving cultural conflicts.”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: So don’t worry if you don’t get it right the first time. The right org structure changes over time as the business and org maturity in growth evolves; what serves you well today may not be the best structure in six months. You almost always encounter new challenges with the existing structure that may warrant a reorg.
